VERDICT: certify

1. `lem-rational-power-laws` — certified.

   - `[L6]` now correctly says: “$0^t=0$ … for $t>0$,” undefined for $t<0$, while preserving `$0^0=1$` ([item](/root/Projects/prestige-math-library/items/lem-rational-power-laws.md:66)).
   - Its cited definition sets `$0^r=0$` for rational `$r>0$` and leaves `$r<0$` undefined ([definition](/root/Projects/prestige-math-library/items/def-rational-power.md:60)). `def-integer-power` defines `$a^0=1$` for every base, including zero ([definition](/root/Projects/prestige-math-library/items/def-integer-power.md:47)), and explicitly adopts `$0^0=1$` ([remark](/root/Projects/prestige-math-library/items/def-integer-power.md:88)).
   - `[L6]` is cited only in step 3.4, where `$r>0$`, and step 4.1, where `$r,s>0$` and hence `$r+s>0$ ([proof](/root/Projects/prestige-math-library/items/lem-rational-power-laws.md:86)). Both remain fully licensed.

2. `def-rational-power` — certified.

   - `rem-real-exponents-deferred` states exactly: “That later development is now published,” identifying `def-real-power` and `thm-real-power-laws` ([remark](/root/Projects/prestige-math-library/items/rem-real-exponents-deferred.md:94)).
   - Both targets exist and have `status: published`. `def-real-power` defines `$a^x:=\exp(x\log a)$` for `$a>0$` and real `$x$ ([definition](/root/Projects/prestige-math-library/items/def-real-power.md:28)); `thm-real-power-laws` supplies the corresponding real-exponent laws ([theorem](/root/Projects/prestige-math-library/items/thm-real-power-laws.md:29)).
   - The replacement bullet is page-local and true: this page constructs rational powers algebraically from roots and integer powers, not through limits, series, or continuity, and it now accurately directs readers to the later real-power development ([replacement](/root/Projects/prestige-math-library/items/def-rational-power.md:89)). It preserves the useful information from the old bullet without the decayed corpus-wide claim.

3. `rem-connectedness-conventions` — certified.

   - The unqualified old condition was vacuous: for every `$x\in U$`, choose `$V=\{x\}$`. The library explicitly declares every one-point space connected ([definition](/root/Projects/prestige-math-library/items/def-connected-space.md:56)), so `$V$` always satisfies connectedness and `$x\in V\subseteq U$`.
   - The repaired condition instead requires `$V$` to be a connected neighbourhood of `$x$`, though not necessarily open ([repair](/root/Projects/prestige-math-library/items/rem-connectedness-conventions.md:64)). This is the standard definition of connectedness im kleinen, and the implication from local connectedness is strict at a point; the standard infinite-broom example satisfies the weaker condition but not local connectedness there. [Literature summary and references](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Locally_connected_space#Connectedness_im_kleinen).
   - The wording is coherent with the inherited convention: a neighbourhood contains an open set around `$x$` but need not itself be open ([definition](/root/Projects/prestige-math-library/items/def-neighbourhood-top.md:47)). Local connectedness requires the connected set itself to be open ([definition](/root/Projects/prestige-math-library/items/def-locally-connected.md:45)).
   - The path-connected analogue also survives: singletons are path-connected under `def-path-connected`, while path connectedness im kleinen likewise requires a path-connected neighbourhood.
